text:
alex.k: heads up — noticed ~6 GPU nodes in preemptible-gpu-pool went NotReady ~15m ago, started seeing a lot of pods stuck Pending with nodeSelector gpu=true

maya: thanks, any obvious kubelet errors?

alex.k: digging now. kubelet shows device plugin reconnects and hostprobe failures. quick excerpt: 
```\nI0324 12:34:56.789 deviceplugin.go:123] failed to dial nvidia-hostprobe at [fe80::1%eth0]:50051: connect: network is unreachable
E0324 12:35:01.102 plugin.go:88] nv-hostprobe: dns resolution returned multiple addresses, picked ipv6, connection refused
```\n
raj: hmm we rolled the kernel bump earlier this week on that pool — could be ipv6 link-local interaction with the hostprobe binding.

lena: also seeing cluster-autoscaler logs with scale-down blocked because Pending pods have gpu resource requests and no nodes available. autoscaler attempted add but many preemptible nodes fail to register fast enough.

oncall-sre: infra-bot flagged a surge in GPU boot time for preemptible pool at 12:20, rolling back won't be instant.

maya: can we get the device-plugin logs from one of the NotReady nodes?

alex.k: grabbing now, here's the device-plugin stderr tail:
```\n2026-03-18T12:22:41Z ERROR nvidia-device-plugin: hostprobe dial tcp [::1]:50051: connect: connection refused
2026-03-18T12:22:45Z WARN  nvidia-device-plugin: host probe returned empty result, retrying
2026-03-18T12:23:12Z INFO  deviceplugin: registering with kubelet
2026-03-18T12:23:13Z ERROR deviceplugin: register failed: rpc error: code = Unavailable desc = connection error
```\n
raj: looks like the plugin is trying IPv6 localhost first (due to /etc/hosts order or DNS returning ::1). The hostprobe binary listens on 127.0.0.1 only after the kernel change. intermittent bind mismatch.

lena: is hostprobe a separate container or binary on host? If container, maybe networkMode changed.

alex.k: hostprobe runs as a sidecar in the daemonset with hostNetwork: true historically, but our 1.3.4 device-plugin image added a multiaddr discovery that prefers v6 if returned.

maya: immediate mitigation: patch daemonset to set env FORCE_IPV4=1 in the device-plugin and hostprobe so it forces 127.0.0.1. That should let nodes register again.

oncall-sre: agreed — patching daemonset now. rolling restart will touch ~120 nodes across zones; preemptibles will bounce.

infra-bot: deploy started by maya. Rolling update strategy: 10% maxUnavailable.

raj: FYI cluster-autoscaler is backed off, but once nodes start reporting allocatable GPUs, scale-up should clear the Pending pods. Could be a ~5-10m recovery.

lena: also temp workaround: add a taint to preemptible-gpu-pool to stop new GPU workloads while we stabilize, then untaint after.

alex.k: applied taint gpu-probe/unstable:NoSchedule to preemptible pool to avoid churn.

maya: daemonset patch deployed, bumped image to 1.3.5-hotfix, env var set. Seeing device-plugin pods go Ready on 4 nodes so far.

raj: removing taint in 10m once we watch healthy nodes populate. CA will start scaling once kubelets report resources.

lena: action items: (1) backport env var to prod image tags, (2) add hostprobe listen fallback to 127.0.0.1 if ::1 connect fails, (3) add a CA check to avoid simultaneous huge register storms.

alex.k: agree. also flagging kernel rollouts for preemptible pool — we should gate the kernel bump behind a device-plugin e2e.

oncall-sre: incident closed for now — nodes recovering, will monitor for 1hr. :thumbsup:

maya: thanks everyone. Can we follow up in changelog and a short postmortem in #postmortems if anything else pops up?

alex.k: will draft a brief root-cause + mitigation note and post in eng-infra and postmortems.

infra-bot: monitor alert: gpu-node-registration-latency resolved at 12:47

maya: great — keeping an eye on cost impact (preemptible churn increased API calls). will ping finance if sustained.
